claims.text: The as-fabricated Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a uniform fcc matrix.
The as-fabricated alloy has minimal initial oxidation.
Elevated-temperature exposure in controlled oxidizing and reducing gases promotes selective oxidation of Al and Ti.
Selective oxidation produces brittle oxide scales or intermetallic compounds.
The brittle phases preferentially form or localize along grain boundaries.
Selective oxidation initially creates protective oxide layers.
The initially protective oxide layers can subsequently become discontinuous or spall.
Reducing conditions can cause the formation of brittle intermetallic phases.
Disrupted oxide scales or brittle intermetallic phases create weak grain-boundary regions.
Weak grain-boundary regions serve as crack-initiation sites.
Crack initiation at these weak regions leads to embrittlement and catastrophic failure.
Exposure at 800–1000°C under the proposed gas environments reduces tensile strength relative to the as-fabricated baseline.
Exposure at 800–1000°C under the proposed gas environments reduces ductility relative to the as-fabricated baseline.
Exposed samples will exhibit non-uniform oxide scales or intergranular intermetallic precipitates.
Oxidizing and reducing environments may produce different detailed degradation pathways but both lead to significant loss of mechanical integrity.
The proposed mechanism applies between 800 and 1000°C when gas compositions are sufficiently oxidizing or reducing to drive selective oxidation or related phase changes.
